title: Make riddles require their clues
problem: Both riddle draws display emoji answers. Picture naming bypasses clue reasoning.
proposal: Use an oral-only riddle stimulus or a scene that does not identify the answer; retain the shown-picture naming mode for naming objectives.
acceptance: Clue-only examples with uniquely defensible answers; the answer cannot be obtained from a pre-answer picture.

title: Reject text in picture stimulus fields
problem: One generated item uses baseEmoji="pillows"; the component displays plain text where a K picture is required.
proposal: Validate emoji/picture fields and regenerate invalid stimuli without fabricating replacements.
acceptance: Every retained item has a real picture stimulus; rejection of plain text is regression-tested.

title: Add picture-pair relationship tasks
problem: Spoken association/opposites/plurals support concepts but do not enact the requested visual matching. word-sorter match_pairs needs Grade 1+ decoding.
proposal: Add separately named visual matching modes for related objects, opposites, locations and morphology; preserve existing spoken production modes.
acceptance: Two visible picture sets, unambiguous valid pairs, no printed-answer dependence, correct/incorrect matching tested.

title: Add contextual K grammar completion
target: di-spoken-practice or a dedicated oral grammar primitive
problem: Articles, pronouns, agreement and tense depend on sentence/discourse context; single-picture naming or noun-only completion cannot certify them.
proposal: Choose the smallest explicit sentence-completion contract after fixing the zero-item pilot. Keep sentence creation distinct from selecting a missing word.
acceptance: Trials for is/are, a/an, pronoun reference and tense with unique contextual keys and non-reader prompts.

title: Make sentence construction accessible at K
problem: Printed word tiles do not establish pictured/audible K access or spontaneous oral sentence production.
proposal: Add pictured, individually audible tiles and task-specific simple/compound/punctuation modes.
acceptance: A pre-reader can identify every tile, construct an SVO sentence, make an error and correct it without reading the answer in a prompt.

title: Make letter formation interactive and scored
problem: Four cumulative letter-formation requirements have no reviewed interactive letter-stroke contract. Two existing LetterTracing displays have no drawing capture or stroke scoring; number and shape tracing assess different forms.
proposal: Reuse existing letter displays and inspect tracing capture infrastructure; add letter-specific input, stroke references, scoring and generator/catalog wiring with uppercase/lowercase cumulative groups and separate trace/copy/write modes.
acceptance: Trace, copy and independently form letters; assess stroke/path coverage with forgiving geometric tolerances and no numeral substitution.

title: Extend the book into print-awareness tasks
problem: Feature locating does not establish directionality, print-unit discrimination, word counting or table-of-contents navigation.
proposal: Add explicit page/text navigation tasks over the actual rendered book.
acceptance: Score left-to-right tracking, letter/word/space identification, word counts, feature purpose and contents-to-page destinations.

title: Separate sound production from recognition/counts
problem: Several curriculum objectives ask for sounds or segmentation; current modes often ask for a menu word or a count and isolate held sounds only.
proposal: Define the honest scored response for each sound family before extending; retain recognition and production as separate mappings.
acceptance: No counting task certifies segmentation production; per-letter/per-sound support and exclusions appear explicitly.

title: Add ending-sound identification
problem: Initial and middle sound modes exist; rhyme and phoneme counts do not identify the final phoneme.
proposal: Add an ending-sound matching task, then consider isolated production only for judgeable sounds.
acceptance: Contrasts differ at their final phoneme; onset/rhyme cues cannot solve every item.

title: Support syllable and onset-rime chunks
problem: Existing blending uses phonemes; syllable-clapper counts beats.
proposal: Represent the chunk unit explicitly and use it in audio cues and accepted responses.
acceptance: cow + boy and c + at preserve their chunk boundaries; word output is judged.

title: Add auditory long/short vowel contrasts
problem: Separate short- and long-vowel decoding modes do not by themselves test discrimination.
proposal: Create paired auditory comparisons with clear vowel contrasts.
acceptance: Student chooses/produces the contrasting vowel without printed silent-e clues doing all the work.

title: Extend early decoding beyond isolated CVC
problem: Inflected/compound reading and contextual near-word discrimination are not covered by morphology transformations alone.
proposal: Add narrowly scoped decoding and word-in-context tasks.
acceptance: Generated inflections/compounds respect K phonics scope and comprehension is assessed separately.

title: Create observable oral-language interactions
problem: Classroom commands, student questions, dialogue and two-minute presentations cannot be graded by a 1-3-word answer pack.
proposal: Start with one bounded two-turn question/clarification task; retain audio and a rubric before expanding to presentations.
acceptance: Questions are student-generated; relevance, turn-taking and intended action are assessed from actual evidence, with teacher observation where necessary.

title: Capture vocabulary in complete child sentences
problem: Single-word frames do not establish use of vocabulary in a self-generated sentence or a multiword scene description.
proposal: Collect short original utterances against a scene or vocabulary set and judge meaning/use, not exact wording.
acceptance: Several valid sentences are accepted; fragments and unrelated memorized sentences do not pass.

title: Add child-authored retelling and expression
problem: Planning choices and ordered event cards do not assess a performed personal story, preference reasons, dialogue or written composition.
proposal: Pilot recorded three-event retelling over a picture plan with teacher-reviewable evidence.
acceptance: Score event sequence and original connected language; clearly separate creative choice from factual correctness.

title: Ground vocabulary and comprehension in scenes
problem: Audio-only recall or hidden answer emoji cannot establish meaning from an actual contextual illustration.
proposal: Attach relevant scenes to a shared story and ask meaning/evidence questions; avoid direct answer pictures for inference.
acceptance: The child must use contextual details and cannot solve the task by naming a single isolated icon.

title: Compare two illustrated stories
problem: Single-story and genre tasks do not compare two stories' characters, settings and event sequences at K.
proposal: Keep two short read-alouds in one context with picture-supported same/different and paired-event tasks.
acceptance: Both texts are referenced, multiple valid comparisons are supported, no advanced reading required.

title: Build semantic webs and chains
problem: Letter-change chains and chronological story arcs cannot represent thematic object relationships.
proposal: Let children connect picture nodes and explain a relation; support a small thematic web and a logical chain.
acceptance: Relations have defensible meaning, unrelated links are rejected or flagged, and multiple valid networks are accepted.

title: Extend spatial scenes beyond fixed placements
problem: Front/behind, self-created scenes and spoken descriptions exceed the current grid contract.
proposal: Add representable scene perspectives and child descriptions while retaining existing place/in/between modes.
acceptance: Every named relation is visually unambiguous and a description is actually elicited when required.

title: Add spatial paths
problem: A static grid explicitly cannot show through/around/across.
proposal: Represent animated traversable paths and judge the child's chosen route.
acceptance: Distinct path relations cannot be satisfied by the same final cell.

title: Verify picture/category coverage in sorting
problem: Spoken labels and emoji cues only partially meet card-sorting requirements and may omit noun kinds or quantity contrasts.
proposal: Test people/places/things and one/many stimuli; add a manipulative response only when the requirement depends on it.
acceptance: Count only visible, unambiguous category examples; state whether the child speaks or moves cards.

title: Collect a reason after sorting
problem: Naming the season does not supply the requested because-reason.
proposal: Add a short item-specific rationale turn following categorization.
acceptance: A correct category with an unrelated reason is not full coverage.

title: Build a K main-idea/detail organizer
problem: Current generic sorting has no shared passage; text-structure analysis expects independent reading.
proposal: Use a read-aloud with picture cards and a central idea/detail web.
acceptance: Distinguish a true supporting detail from a related but unstated distractor and retain links to the story.

title: Add prediction and evidence-source tasks
problem: Existing modes explain or recall what happened; predictions, morals and stated/inferred distinctions need separate tasks.
proposal: Add before-reveal predictions and evidence-source questions.
acceptance: Questions are asked before the outcome is revealed and plausible alternative reasoning is handled explicitly.

title: Use picture events for K story ordering
problem: Current arc events are text cards; K picture ordering must be demonstrated.
proposal: Attach scene images and read-aloud to event cards.
acceptance: A non-reader can order 3-4 supplied story events and label beginning/middle/end.

title: Contrast two meanings of one word
problem: One missing noun does not establish multiple meanings of bat or run.
proposal: Generate two contextual scenes for the same surface word.
acceptance: The child identifies which meaning applies and sees both senses represented.

title: Collect a three-word rhyme family
problem: One rhyme response does not build a retained family of three distinct words.
proposal: Extend open production with a small collection and duplicate checking.
acceptance: Three distinct valid words, with fair acceptance of unlisted rhymes.

title: Verify emotion vocabulary from pictures
problem: Feeling inference is available, but facial/situational vocabulary requires valid emotion scenes.
proposal: Probe clear faces and situations and reject ambiguous or merely named emotions.
acceptance: Stimuli support the intended emotion and near-synonyms are accepted.

title: Recall three details from one presentation
problem: Multiple short stories do not demonstrate retaining three details from a single oral presentation.
proposal: Use one shared presentation with three independent recall questions.
acceptance: Each answer references a different supplied detail, with no clue leakage across questions.

title: Clarify broad activity requirements
problem: Participation and generic vocabulary activities do not specify which measurable action establishes mastery.
proposal: Propose explicit action/evidence clauses while preserving source text and IDs until approved.
acceptance: A reviewer can tell what student response would satisfy or fail the requirement.
